chapter: Band personalities, Duke's last years and the office
title: Taking cornbread and beef stew to Duke in hospital and hotel
summary: Rose took cornbread to Duke at St. Vincent's and beef stew to the Beverly Wilshire.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And Rose was talking about when he was in the hospital here in 1973, at St. Vincent's -- and what happened, Rose?
He called here; or had the nurse call, and asked me -- Marie Cole and I went down to see him, and

then he called back again, and asked me would I bring him some cornbread, because he couldn't get cornbread there, so Juan and I went to see him to give him the cornbread, and then when he left the hospital and went to the Beverly Wilshire Hotel to live, he called and asked me would I make him a beef stew and make him some cornbread and bring it out there, so naturally, I made the beef stew and I made the cornbread and I took it out there to him, and I said, 'Well, I think I will have some of your beef stew and cornbread.' And he said, 'No, you order your dinner; I want this for myself. I want this'.
So we ate out there, didn't we, Juan? We ate out there that evening, didn't we, at the Beverly Wilshire?
Yeah, I think we ate in his room, didn't we?

Well, anyway, he told me to order dinner, but evidently I didn't order dinner, as Juan said; we came home afterwards, because different ones began to come in. I tell you who came in -- what was that guy's name who is in the swimming pool business?
Bob Yutak and his wife came in, and we didn't stay very long afterwards; we came home.
You mentioned off the tape how you
felt walking in to the Beverly Wilshire with a pot of beef stew and cornbread!

Oh yeah, with beef stew and cornbread; I felt kind of silly walking in to the Beverly Wilshire Hotel with that under my arm, you know? But of course, nobody knew what I had, but I still had it, and you know, I knew what I had so I felt kind of stupid.
Well, Duke had a way of putting people in to unusual circumstances.
